correctness.rationale: The equation is σ(n)/n=2x/(x+1), with the right side strictly increasing for positive integral x. For distinct odd primes p<q, the left side is (1+1/p)(1+1/q), strictly greater than 1 and bounded above by (1+1/3)(1+1/5)=8/5, with equality only at (3,5). This gives x∈{2,3,4} and settles x=4 directly. At x=3 one would have 2σ(n)=3n, impossible for odd n. At x=2 the frozen factorization (p−3)(q−3)=12 has positive even factors and only the ordered pair (2,6), giving q=9. For n=p², p=3 gives σ/(2n−σ)=13/5; for p≥5, σ/n=1+1/p+1/p² lies strictly between 1 and 4/3, so cannot equal 2x/(x+1). Finally 15 has σ=24 and x=4. Thus both possible multiplicity-two cases are exhausted without an upper bound on n. The certificate is a summary of the branches; the script checks finite divisions and inequalities and a regression through 200000, not the unbounded quantifier. No fresh script execution or formal verification is claimed.
residual_risks: No claim beyond odd semiprimes in this reciprocal-abundancy set.
